claims.text: A silicon-infusion pretreatment that forms a thin, continuous silica-rich oxide layer improves the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
Pack siliconizing can incorporate silicon into the near-surface region of boride-based components.
Typical hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions permit oxidation and formation of a silica-rich layer.
Silicon infusion causes silicon segregation and oxidation at the component surface.
Silicon segregation and oxidation produce a continuous, thin silica-rich surface oxide.
The silica-rich oxide acts as a protective barrier against molten aluminum.
The silica-rich barrier reduces aluminum diffusion into the boride-based substrate.
The silica-rich barrier limits interfacial reactions between molten aluminum and the substrate.
Silicon-treated components will corrode at a lower rate than untreated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
The protective effect persists only while the silica-rich layer remains continuous and intact.
Mechanical abrasion can compromise the effectiveness of the silica-rich protective layer.
Chemical impurities can compromise the effectiveness of the silica-rich protective layer.
Non-uniform silicon treatment can compromise corrosion protection.
